Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

package Problems_On_Number_System;

import java.util.Scanner;

public class OctalToBinary {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Scanner sc = new Scanner(System.in);
        System.out.println("enter the octal value:");
        String s = sc.nextLine();
        int decimal = 0;
        int pow = 0;
        for (int i = s.length() - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
            int val = s.charAt(i) - '0';
            decimal += (val * Math.pow(8, pow));
            pow++;
        }
        System.out.println(decimal);
        // now decimal to binary conversion
        String bin = "";
        while (decimal > 0) {
            int remainder = decimal % 2;
            bin = remainder + bin;
            decimal = decimal / 2;
        }
        System.out.println("the binary value is " + bin);
        sc.close();
    }

}
